summary: High rate of 429s when sending concurrent embedding batch requests via SDK
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden spike in 429 throttling responses when sending concurrent batch embedding requests using the official SDK. Impact: Customer's indexing job for search vectors is failing intermittently; estimated ~40% of requests returning 429s over several hours; downstream pipeline delayed. Environment: Production, ClearLens account on Dedicated pool in us-east-1. Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:25 UTC - first report from customer; 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - support triaged and asked for logs; 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - SRE looped in; 2026-03-11 02:15 UTC - engineering rolled a mitigation config; 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - root cause confirmed and fix deployed.

Key ask: Determine why customer is receiving 429s despite being on dedicated capacity and provide mitigation and permanent fix.

Expected behavior: Dedicated customers with reserved GPU capacity should not be subject to global per-API-key request throttles for steady-state batch embedding workloads.

Observed behavior: Intermittent 429 responses tied to short bursts in concurrency; 5–10 second windows of high 429 rates during customer batch ingestion runs.

Customer-provided context: Customer uses the Python SDK (v1.8.2) with parallel worker processes (8 workers), each sending embedding batches of 256 texts. They observed failures starting yesterday during a scheduled reindex job.
steps_to_reproduce: Create 8 parallel worker processes that call client.embeddings.create with batch_size=256
Run all workers concurrently against the customer API key for the ClearLens account in us-east-1
Observe 429 responses returned intermittently in ~40% of requests during peak concurrency
customer_notes: ClearLens: 'We had this same pipeline running last week without issues. Nothing changed on our side except scaling up batch_size from 128 to 256.'
ClearLens: 'We rely on predictable throughput; can you confirm whether dedicated pools still have global rate limits?'
comments: 2026-03-10T09:42 - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Collected SDK logs and asked for sample request IDs. Looping SRE. (sla: P1)
2026-03-10T10:08 - Priya Rao (SRE): Observed token-bucket exhaustion on API gateway for org org_cll_22. Burst capacity depleted. Adding SRE to investigate quota configs.

2026-03-10T11:30 - Miguel Torres (Engineer): Hypothesis: SDK v1.8.2 sends a per-request 'tokens' header computed from batch_size which increments gateway consumption; doubling batch_size increased token weight. Checking rate limiter code path and dedicated pool exceptions.
2026-03-11T02:20 - Miguel Torres (Engineer): Temporary mitigation applied: increased org-level burst allowance for pool-42 for next 24 hours; asked customer to resume reindex and report back.
2026-03-11T03:05 - ClearLens (Customer): Reindex resumed. 429s dropped to <2% during the observed window. Confirming throughput returned to acceptable levels.

2026-03-12T09:40 - Miguel Torres (Engineer): Root cause identified. Preparing permanent fix; will roll out rate-limiter logic to exempt dedicated-pool traffic from per-api-key burst deduction when quota configured at pool level.
2026-03-12T14:05 - Miguel Torres (Engineer): Fix deployed behind feature flag to production; monitoring for regressions. Marking ticket resolved after 24-hour observation period.
investigation: Summary: Initial logs showed the API gateway's token bucket consistently hitting zero for org_cll_22 during concurrent batch runs. The dedicated pool was healthy (GPU utilization normal) so serving-runtime was not the bottleneck. We reviewed the rate-limiter implementation: a recent change (PR #4812) unintentionally counted dedicated-pool routed requests against both the pool quota AND the org-level API-key bucket, effectively double-charging burst tokens when batch_size (token weight) increased. Evidence: request traces showing x-pool-route=pool-42 and gateway bucket depletion events aligned with customer requests. Additional evidence in grafana: /dashboards/rate-limiter?org=org_cll_22 shows synchronous drops in gateway tokens matching the customer's job start time. Hypothesis confirmed by reproducer: running emulator with batch_size=256 and pool-routing header replicated the 429 spike; when we mocked the previous rate-limiter behavior the 429s disappeared.
resolution: Root cause: Double-accounting in rate-limiter for dedicated-pool routed traffic after a recent change to token accounting. Permanent fix: updated rate-limiter to prioritize pool-level quota when a request is routed to a dedicated pool (PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4887). Deployed change 2026-03-12 13:50 UTC behind a feature flag, validated in canary, then promoted to production. Mitigation applied during investigation: temporarily increased org-level burst allowance for pool-42. Postfix: asked customer to upgrade SDK to v1.9.0 which includes improved client-side retry backoff and a 'preferred-pool' hint that reduces gateway accounting. Follow-up items: add e2e test for pool-routing accounting, update runbook to include dedicated-pool throttling checks, and schedule a short postmortem to document sequence and rollout plan. Customer outcome: ClearLens confirmed their job runs completed successfully and we issued a credit for affected API usage.
